Unmarried children under 18 can be eligible to receive Social Security benefits when you die.

Children can get benefits at any age if disabled before age 22 and remaining disabled.
Natural children, stepchildren, grandchildren, step-grandchildren, or adopted children may receive benefits under certain circumstances.
Eligible children receive 75 percent of your basic benefit amount.

Widow or widower, full retirement age or older: 100 percent of your benefit amount
Widow or widower, age 60 to full retirement age: 71 to 99 percent of your basic amount
Disabled widow or widower, age 50 through 59: 71 percent
Widow or widower, any age, caring for a child under age 16: 75 percent
Reduced benefits as early as age 60 or full benefits at full retirement age or older
Benefits as early as age 50 if disabled AND disability started before or within seven years of your death
Benefits at any age, if not remarried, and taking care of your child who is under age 16 or disabled and receives benefits on your record
